newsitem.title: INDIA: New eastern Indian port to be commissioned in Oct.
newsitem.headline: New eastern Indian port to be commissioned in Oct.

text.p: A new deep water port with a draft of 9.5 metres at Kakinada on the eastern coast is expected to be commissioned next month, the chief minister of the southern Andhra Pradesh state said.
Kakinada is a natural harbour and a major fishing centre.
The existing harbour handled 2.23 million tonnes of cargo during 1995/96 (April-March), a statement by chief minister Chandrababu Naidu tabled in the state assembly on Thursday said.
As many as 217 ships called at the port during the year, yielding a revenue of 68.61 million rupees for the state government, officials said.

The deep water port has a capacity to handle three million tonnes of cargo annually. The new port cost $97.4 million, for which ADB has contributed $77.9 million. The balance cost is borne by the Andhra Pradesh government.
